Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testAxisFollowing` uses an XPath expression with `following::node()` and expects it to match any type of node, specifically the second node following the second `location` node. The current bug report indicates that in `DOMNodePointer.java` line 120, the method implementing node test for `node()` (likely the static method `testNode(Node, NodeTest)`) only matches `Node.ELEMENT_NODE` and `Node.DOCUMENT_NODE` types when the node test type `Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE` is encountered:

```java
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE :
    return nodeType == Node.ELEMENT_NODE ||
           nodeType == Node.DOCUMENT_NODE;
```

However, the XPath `node()` test should match any node type, not just element or document nodes.

The method `testNode(Node node, NodeTest test)` confirms this behavior, where different node tests return true only for specific node types. The relevant case for `node()` only checks for element and document nodes, excluding text nodes, comment nodes, processing instructions, etc.

The issue report proposes replacing this with `return true;` for `Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE` to reflect matching any node type.

This explains the failure of test `testAxisFollowing()` which expects `following::node()` to consider any node type, but the current code restricts it. This mapping for `Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE` is likely incorrect according to XPath semantics and causes the test failure.

Recent bug reports about node sets and iterators do not directly address this specific issue of node type matching.

In summary, the root cause is an incorrect node type check for the `node()` test in `DOMNodePointer.testNode(Node, NodeTest)`, which should return true for any node instead of limiting to element and document nodes only.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
